description:
PearCinema plays the film and television collection on a machine you own - an Umbrel, a NAS, an old desktop - from anywhere, over a direct encrypted connection between your phone and that machine.

  No port forwarding, no VPN, no dynamic DNS, no account, and no copy of your library in anyone's cloud. Your files never leave your hardware: they stream through the live connection while they play, and you can skip to any point in a film without downloading it first.

  PLEASE READ FIRST

PearCinema needs that machine running the free PearCinema host, which is the source of the films. It is not a player for files stored on your phone. So that you can look around before you have one, the app comes with four short public-domain films and nothing else. If you do not have a server yet, someone else can let you into theirs.

  PEARCINEMA PROVIDES NO CONTENT

PearCinema is a player for files you already have. It hosts nothing, indexes nothing and has no catalogue of its own. The four public-domain films it ships with are the whole of what comes in the box: there is nothing else in it to search for, browse or download, and no way to obtain a film through it.

  READS THE LIBRARY YOU ALREADY HAVE

  Point the host at a Jellyfin or Emby server you already run and PearCinema uses its library, its artwork, its seasons and its episodes. Point it at a plain folder of files instead and PearCinema reads them itself: it works out films from shows, sorts episodes into seasons, and picks up the descriptions and posters that Kodi, Sonarr or Radarr already left on the disk. So a folder is a real library rather than a list of filenames.

  IT MAKES YOUR FILES PLAY

Files your phone can already handle go straight through untouched. Anything it cannot, the machine holding the films repackages or converts as you watch, using its own graphics chip, so it costs that machine very little and never changes your original file. Subtitles come along, including the picture subtitles from discs.

  IN THE APP

  - Browse films and shows with posters, descriptions and episode thumbnails
  - Search the whole library
  - Carry on where you stopped, and when an episode ends the next one is offered
  - Resume points and favourites that follow you between your own devices
  - Everyone in the house has their own list rather than sharing yours
  - Downloads: keep a film on the phone for a flight, converted in advance if your device needs it
  - Send a film to a Roku or a Samsung television and drive it from your lock screen
  - Pair with more than one machine and they look like one library
  - Ask the owner for something you cannot find, and see what they did with it

  THE LIBRARY DOES NOT HAVE TO BE YOURS

  Someone can let a friend or a family member in, each as their own person with their own devices, their own place in whatever they were watching, and no login to pass around. The owner sees every device and can revoke one, or everything one person holds, within seconds - mid-film, not on next login, and it stops a television that device had started. Nobody who is let in ever receives a copy of a file.

  PAIRING IS ONE SCAN

  Scan a QR code and you are in. There is no password, no server address and no account to create. The connection itself proves which device is calling, so there is no token to leak, copy or forget to rotate.

  WHEN A DIRECT CONNECTION IS NOT POSSIBLE

  Some mobile networks and locked-down wifi refuse a direct connection between two devices. When that happens PearCinema can fall back to a relay run by PeerLoom, which forwards encrypted data it cannot read and keeps no copy of it. Your phone always tries a direct connection first, and while a film is coming through the relay its quality is held down so that watching away from home does not quietly consume a data plan.

  OPEN SOURCE

PearCinema is MIT licensed and developed in the open. The host you run on your own machine is free, and so is the app.
promotionalText: The films on a machine you own, playable anywhere. No port forwarding, no VPN, no account, and no copy of your library in anyone's cloud.
whatsNew:
# PearCinema 1.1.0

Your film and television collection, playable anywhere, without exposing your server to
the internet.

PearCinema plays video straight off a computer you own: an Umbrel, a NAS, an old desktop.
Your phone reaches it directly over an encrypted connection. No port forwarding, no VPN,
no dynamic DNS, no account, and no copy of your files on anyone else's server.

And that machine does not have to be yours. If a friend or a family member lets you into
theirs, their library simply appears in your app, with no login handed out and nothing
copied.

## Getting started

1. Install the host on the machine with your films (macOS, Windows, Linux, Umbrel or Docker).
2. Open the dashboard and point it at your library.
3. Scan the QR code with the app on your phone. That is the setup.

## What you can do

Watch your library from anywhere. Browse films and shows with posters, descriptions and
episode thumbnails, search the whole collection, and skip to any point in a film without
downloading it first. When an episode ends the next one is offered.

Watch it here too. The dashboard is a player, so any laptop or desktop on your network can
open the library and start a film without installing anything.

Let people in, and cut them off. Access is per person and per device: your phone, your
tablet, a friend. Revoke any one of them without disturbing the others, and it takes
effect within seconds, mid-film rather than on next login. It also stops a television that
device had started. Guest passes expire on their own after a time you set.

Take films with you. Keep a film on the phone for a flight, converted in advance if your
device needs it.

Pick up where you left off. Resume points and watchlists follow you between your own
devices, and everyone you let in has their own rather than sharing yours.

Send it to a television. Play on a Roku or a Samsung and drive it from your phone's lock
screen.

More than one library at once. If you are let into several, they blend into one.

Ask for something you cannot find. Anyone you have let in can request a film, and the
owner works through the queue in the app.

## Your films, wherever they already live

Point the host at a Jellyfin or an Emby server you already run and PearCinema uses its
library, artwork, seasons and episodes. Point it at a plain folder of files instead and it
reads them itself: it works out films from shows, sorts episodes into seasons, and picks
up the descriptions and posters that Kodi, Sonarr or Radarr already left on the disk. So a
folder is a real library rather than a list of filenames, and it needs no internet lookup
and no account with anyone.

## It makes your files play

Files your phone can already handle go straight through untouched. Anything it cannot, the
machine holding the films repackages or converts as you watch, using its own graphics chip
(Intel, AMD, NVIDIA or Apple), so it costs that machine very little and never changes your
original file. Subtitles come along, including the picture subtitles from discs, which are
drawn onto the film where a phone cannot show them by itself.

## Staying connected

Most of the time your phone talks straight to your host. Some mobile carriers and
locked-down wifi refuse a direct connection, and PearCinema then falls back to a relay run
by PeerLoom. The relay only passes along traffic that is already encrypted: it can see
that your device is talking to your host and how much data moves, never what is in it, and
it keeps no copy. While a film is coming through the relay its quality is held down so
that watching away from home does not quietly consume a data plan. You can turn the relay
off, or paste in your own.

## Keeping it running

On Linux the host installs as a proper background service: your library keeps serving
after you log out and starts again by itself when the machine reboots. On macOS and
Windows it runs while you are signed in.

## Downloads

| Your machine | File |
| --- | --- |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `PearCinema-1.1.0-arm64.dmg` |
| macOS (Intel) | `PearCinema-1.1.0.dmg` |
| Windows | `PearCinema-Setup-1.1.0.exe` |
| Linux | `PearCinema-1.1.0.AppImage` or `pearcinema-desktop_1.1.0_amd64.deb` |
| Android | `pearcinema-v1.1.0.apk` |
| Umbrel | Add the PeerLoom community app store and install from there |

The macOS app is signed and notarized by Apple, so it opens normally.

Windows will show a warning. The installer is not signed with a certificate yet, so
SmartScreen says "unknown publisher". Choose More info, then Run anyway.

## Good to know

- PearCinema provides no content. It is a player for files you already have: it hosts
  nothing, indexes nothing and has no catalogue of its own.
- The phone apps are not in the app stores yet. iOS is with App Review; on Android,
  install the `.apk` above or get it on Zapstore.
- On Linux the `.deb` sets up the background service for you. The AppImage can do the same
  with `--install-service`, and otherwise runs when you log in.
- On an Umbrel, plug an external drive in and PearCinema can see it, including a drive
  connected after the app started.
- The host tells you where to find new versions, but does not update itself yet.
